To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the YO dye binds to dsDNA in a similar way as it binds to the alternating polynucleartides [poly(dG-dC)]2 and [Poly(dA-dT)]2.
the YO monomers bind in an intercalating mode to both AT and GC basepairs, and that YOYO binds to dsDNA with the same orientation as the YO units in the dimer.
YO is an intercalating dye and that YOYO is a bisintercalating dye.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the binding of the dye YO to [pol dAT)2 and [poly dGC)]2, and the fluorescent properties of the YO‐YOYO‐DNA system.
the interaction of the fluorescent dye Y‐base with DNA and its analogs.
the binding of Yoyo and YO to dsDNA and the fluorescent properties of the YOYO and YO‐dsDNA complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
YO and YOOY bind to AT and GC pairs in dsDNA by intercalation at low dye concentrations.
YO and Yoyo bind to dsDNA by intercalation and by external binding, and that the intercalated dye is located in the minor groove.
YO and Yoyo are intercalators of double‐stranded AT and GC DNA, as well as the double‐stranded alternating polynucleotide duplexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
YO and YY bind to AT and GC pairs in a similar way, and that the binding to AT pairs is stronger.
YOYO is a good fluorescent probe for dsDNA.
YO binds to dsDNA with a high preference for the major groove.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding mode of YO and of the dimer YOO is not affected by the sequence of the polynucleotide.
YOYO is an excellent probe for the characterization of the secondary structure of dsDNA, as well as for the characterization of its interaction with other molecules.
YO and YYO are good probes for studying the structure of AT‐rich and GC‐rich DNA.
